title: The Wages of Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The wages of sin means that sin earns death, judgment, and separation from God apart from salvation in Christ. Sin is not merely damaging; it deserves righteous consequence before God.
summary: The wages of sin means that sin earns death, judgment, and separation from God apart from salvation in Christ. Sin is not merely damaging; it deserves righteous consequence before God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ took the wages of sin upon Himself for His people and gives eternal life as the gift of God. In Him, death is defeated and judgment is answered for all who believe.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Sin pays wages. Scripture teaches that rebellion against God leads to death. This includes spiritual death, physical death, and final judgment for those who remain outside Christ.

The wages of sin are not random consequences. God warned from the beginning that disobedience brings death. Sin separates people from the God who is life, and judgment follows because God is holy and just.

People may try to minimize sin by focusing only on immediate consequences. But Scripture looks deeper and farther. Sin’s final end is not embarrassment, regret, or difficulty; it is death and judgment before God.

The Gospel shines against this dark reality. The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord. Christ bears judgment and gives life to those who trust Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If sin’s wages are denied, urgency disappears. People may treat sin as manageable, amusing, or private while ignoring its eternal seriousness. Scripture speaks plainly so sinners will flee to Christ.

This doctrine is also merciful because it tells the truth before final judgment comes. God warns sinners not to destroy them with fear, but to call them to the Savior who gives life freely.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take sin’s end seriously. Do not measure sin only by whether it causes immediate pain. Turn to Christ for eternal life, warn others with humility and love, and live with gratitude that Jesus has borne what sin deserved for all who trust Him.
